sentences.text: The learned High Court Government Pleader takes notice for the respondent No.1/State.

2. Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.
3.
This petition is filed under section 438 of Cr.P.C. by accused Nos.2 to 5 in Crime No.608/2023 registered at Whitefield Police Station, Bengaluru city.
4. The complaint is lodged by one Pavan kumar S/o.
late Rudra munigowda, the brother of deceased Smt.Chatira.

In the complaint he has alleged that his deceased sister was given in marriage to accused No.1, Dhananjaya about 8 years prior to the date of incident and at the time of marriage,
gold ornaments and a site was given as dowry.
In their wedlock, couple has two children.
Accused No.1 was addicted to alcohol and he was subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture.

He has sold the site and the gold ornaments which were given NC: 2024:KHC:5747 at the time of marriage and since the deceased had questioned the same, all the accused were subjecting her to torture and therefore, she consumed poison on 14.12.2023.
5. Initially, case was registered against accused Nos.1 to 5 for the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The victim was admitted to hospital for treatment, but died on 21.12.2023.

Hence, the police submitted a requisition to include Section 306 of IPC.
6.
The petitioners / accused Nos.2 to 5 are the mother, brothers and father of accused No.1.
In the complaint, allegations are made against them that when the deceased questioned about the sale of site by accused No.1, all the accused have subjected her to physical and mental torture.

The specific allegations are against accused No.1 that he was addicted to alcohol and NC: 2024:KHC:5747 subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture and that he has sold the site and the gold ornaments.

7. The learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the deceased has committed suicide in her parental home in Bengaluru, where she was living for more than one month and the petitioners were not living along with the deceased, but they are living separately.

It is also her contention that, as per sale deed, even the deceased has signed the documents and therefore, it cannot be said that, the site was sold without her consent.
8.
There are no specific allegations against the petitioners, who are the parents-in-law and brothers-in- law of the deceased.
Further, according to the petitioners counsel, they are residing separately.
They have undertaken to co-operate with the investigation of the case.
Hence, by imposing necessary conditions.
The relief sought by the petitioners can be granted.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:5747 ORDER Mrs. Rathnamma vs State By Whitefield Police Station on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47895368/
3 i) Petition is allowed.

sentences.text:
ii) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 5 in Crime No.608/2023 of Whitefield Police Station shall be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest, subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two sureties for the likesum.
b) They shall furnish proof of their residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
c) They shall be available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) They shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till completion of the investigation of the case.
NC: 2024:KHC:5747 e) They shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
f) They shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
